pr_comments: Can someone please explain what are golden files which cause the ci set up to fail
@IgorMinar @alxhub @pkozlowski-opensource @jelbourn why is component repo unit tests failing and how to make them right there is nothing about this in developer.md in the repo

@ajitsinghkaler see: https://github.com/angular/components/blob/master/src/cdk/scrolling/virtual-for-of.ts#L25 - looks like CDK is using `NgIterable` - which tells me that this is a public API (at least in practice) and we can't / should not remove it right now? I guess we should still make all the changes but keep the `NgIterable` and deprecate it.

As this touches the generic type constraint of `NgForOf`, we'd have to verify that it does not cause a de-opt in the type checker that was achieved in #34021. I.e. changing `U extends NgIterable` to `U extends Iterable` may de-opt as `Iterable` is a global ambient type.

@JoostK are there any tests that are testing the functionality because no tests are failing. 

If there are no tests should we add tests too

@ajitsinghkaler There is _no_ test for ambient type support at the moment. We should definitely add such a test in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/test/type_parameter_emitter_spec.ts` to verify that it behaves as desired. Let me know if you need more info on that, I can help out if needed.

# 🚀 feature request

### Relevant Package
<!-- Can you pin-point one or more @angular/* packages the are relevant for this feature request? -->
<!-- ✍️edit: --> This feature request is for @angular/core


### Description


```
type NgIterable<T> = Array<T> | Iterable<T>;
```

Please change it into

```
type NgIterable<T> = ReadonlyArray<T> | Iterable<T>;
```
comments: I'm confused by this in general, since Array<T> is already a subtype of Iterable<T>.

I'm also confused by this in general, since Array is already a subtype of Iterable.
This type was introduced by @alxhub in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/33536. Perhaps he can explain why it was necessary to us a union of array and iterable?

Actually I have no idea why `NgIterable` is defined that way. #33536 just adds the type to `fake_core`, its real definition is in `iterable_differs.ts` and as far as I can tell it's been that way for a long time. My suspicion is something related to `Iterable` was different in the older TypeScript versions from when `NgIterable` was defined, that required the redundant definition.

Sorry I git-blamed @alxhub unfairly. As he points out, his commit is different.

Here is possibly some more context:

https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/14104/files#r98477745

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/4.0.0-beta.5/modules/@angular/core/src/change_detection/differs/iterable_differs.ts#L29

```
// TODO(misko): We can't use Iterable as it would break the .d.ts file for ES5 users.
```

Closing as `ReadonlyArray` is supported through the `Iterable` type, and type flowing into `NgForOfContext.ngForOf` retains the readonly array type as expected: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-xpnnjw?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts (change the signature of `test` to just `string[]` instead of `readonly string[]` to see an error, which confirms that `NgForOfContext.ngForOf` is indeed a readonly array).
